title: Sponsor-driven fast-track and deferred review queue for model catalog submissions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Enterprise customers and partner teams increasingly request expedited model onboarding (pinning, new-adds, variant rollouts) under a sponsorship agreement. Today these requests are handled ad-hoc by PMs and Platform Engineers, leading to inconsistent SLAs, unclear audit trails, and missed safety/eval checks.

Goals:
- Create a documented sponsor-driven fast-track lane that allows high-trust customers to request an accelerated onboarding path while preserving critical eval and safety gates.
- Add a deferred review queue for lower-priority/exploratory model suggestions that preserves signal without consuming immediate engineering capacity.
- Define explicit SLAs, acceptance criteria, and operational steps for both lanes so product, eng, and security know when to expedite vs defer.

Proposed approach:
1) Intake form changes: add "Sponsor ID" and "Business Impact" fields to the model request form and expose a checkbox to request fast-track. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/MC/Sponsor+Fasttrack+Spec
2) Fast-track criteria: sponsor confirmed + business impact >= "high" + security checklist signoff (PM or Security). Requests passing criteria get a "fast-track" tag and an SLA of 10 business days for onboarding decision and 30 business days for full catalog placement.
3) Deferred queue: non-fast-track suggestions with low/medium impact go into a deferred queue monitored weekly. Owners can nominate items for a monthly "catalog refresh" batch.
4) Eval gating: every fast-track request still requires a minimal eval run (regression tests on defined prompt suite) and a short human review. Deployed model variants must include fallback routing for 7 days post-rollout.
5) Audit and notifications: all steps recorded in the request ticket; automated Slack notifications to #catalog-ops for fast-track events and a weekly digest for deferred queue items.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form accepts sponsor ID and fast-track option and surfaces the criteria to requesters.
- Fast-track SLA enforced in routing rules and measurable in the console dashboard.
- Deferred queue exists and is visible to PMs with filtering by label and submitter.
- Minimal eval runner integrated into the onboarding checklist with pass/fail recorded on ticket.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Ship form and tags; update internal runbook.
- Week 2: Configure routing rules and Slack alerts.
- Week 3: Pilot with 2 sponsored customers and iterate.
- Week 6: Graduate to default workflow and include in catalog-2026.04 release notes.

Metrics to monitor:
- Time-to-decision for fast-track requests (target <= 10 business days).
- Percentage of fast-track requests that hit all eval gates (target >= 90%).
- Deferred queue backlog and nominations per month.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Fast-track could create perceived unfairness; mitigated by clear public criteria and quarterly transparency report.
- Accelerating onboarding may increase regression risk; mitigated by mandatory minimal eval suite and temporary routing controls.

Open questions:
- Do sales sponsors need a separate SLA commitment documented in contracts? (Legal + Sales input required)
- Thresholds for "business impact" need a numeric rubric.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/MC/Sponsor+Fasttrack+Spec
- Intake form draft: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1fakexxx
- Example fast-track ticket (mock): https://linear.redwood.com/PM-46820-mock
- GitHub PR for intake UI change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7281
